findings.claim: Every lesson's sixth practice question is labelled '20 marks — Evaluate an Interpretation (with SPaG)', with a band ladder of [16–20 + up to 4 SPaG] / [11–15 + 2–3] / [6–10 + 1–2] / [1–5 + 0–1]. All 14 lessons.
findings.truth: On Paper 3 the interpretation question is worth 16 marks, with up to 4 SPaG marks awarded separately on top (Section B = 8 + 4 + 4 + 16 + 4 SPaG = 36). The ladder as written gives up to 20 content marks and then adds 4 more, and it teaches students that the paper carries both a 16-mark and a 20-mark interpretation question. Relabelled to 16 marks and the ladder rebuilt as 13–16 / 9–12 / 5–8 / 1–4 with the SPaG tiers kept.
findings.evidence: specs/edexcel/history-1HI0.md, Paper 3 assessment section (Section A 16 marks, Section B 36 marks of which up to 4 in Q3(d) are for SPaG)

findings.claim: Exam tips in lessons 3, 9, 10, 11 and 12 tell students to lock in SPaG marks 'on the 20-mark question', and lesson 3 refers to '16- and 20-mark interpretation questions'.
findings.truth: There is only one interpretation essay on Paper 3 and it is 16 marks; the 4 SPaG marks sit outside the 16.

findings.claim: Nineteen invented claims about examiner behaviour across all 14 lessons: 'examiners reward students who...', 'examiners want to see...', 'Examiner reports for Paper 3 modern depth options reward answers that...', 'examiners specifically penalise answers that drift into source-style analysis', and 'the Edexcel Paper 3 examiner reports both warn against this'.
findings.truth: None of this is documented; two of them cite examiner reports that are not quoted or checkable, and one asserts a penalty no mark scheme contains. All rewritten in the site's own voice ('strong answers...', 'top-band answers...') with the advice itself kept.
findings.evidence: house rule on fabricated examiner claims; specs/edexcel/history-1HI0.md carries no such statements

findings.claim: 'the historian Sun Shuyun and the Historical Association both stress that the heroic narrative was built afterwards'.
findings.truth: Sun Shuyun's The Long March (2006) does argue this. Attributing the same position to the Historical Association is an invented citation; the attribution has been dropped.

findings.claim: Knowledge check 3: 'By 1945, the Guomindang government had received around _____ in US aid since the start of the Sino-Japanese War' — answer $3 billion.
findings.truth: The lesson's own text gives c.$3 billion as aid for 1945–49, not aid received by 1945. The stem has been re-dated to 1945–49 to match.
findings.evidence: internal contradiction with the lesson's content_html

findings.claim: 'Three weeks later, the Huaihai Campaign opened in central China' — following the end of the Liaoshen Campaign.
findings.truth: Liaoshen ended on 2 November 1948 and Huaihai opened on 6 November 1948: four days, not three weeks.

findings.claim: 'Mao explicitly defended the bloodshed: ‘A revolution is not a dinner party.’' — placed in the 1950–52 land reform.
findings.truth: The quotation is genuine but comes from Mao's 1927 Report on an Investigation of the Peasant Movement in Hunan, twenty-three years earlier. The date has been added so the attribution is honest.
findings.evidence: Mao, Report on an Investigation of the Peasant Movement in Hunan (1927)

findings.claim: 'Frank Dikötter calls it ‘tofu-dreg metal’' — repeated as a flashcard question and answer.
findings.truth: Dikötter describes backyard-furnace output as useless in Mao's Great Famine, but this quoted phrase cannot be verified as his. The judgement has been kept and the attribution removed.
findings.evidence: no verifiable source for the phrase in Dikötter

findings.claim: After the 7,000 Cadres Conference of January 1962: 'He later told Edgar Snow he had begun, even then, to plan a second cultural revolution.'
findings.truth: Mao's remark to Edgar Snow (1970) dated his decision that Liu Shaoqi had to go to January 1965, not to 1962. The sentence has been deleted rather than re-dated.

findings.claim: HTML <em> tags inside plain-text JSON fields: lesson 8 (two flashcard answers and two practice mark schemes), lesson 12 (two flashcard answers), lesson 14 (one knowledge check stem).
findings.truth: These fields are plain text, so the tags render as literal '<em>' on the page. Tags stripped; the lesson-14 title now uses quotation marks.
findings.evidence: house convention: *_html fields use entities, plain-text fields use unicode

findings.claim: 'The orthodox CCP ‘70 per cent right, 30 per cent wrong’ verdict (1981) treats the Cultural Revolution as an honest mistake by an ageing leader.'
findings.truth: The 1981 Resolution's 70/30 judgement was on Mao's whole career. The same Resolution condemned the Cultural Revolution outright as the heaviest losses suffered by the party, the state and the people since 1949. A student writing that the CCP judged the Cultural Revolution 70 per cent right would lose marks on an interpretations question.
findings.evidence: CCP Resolution on Certain Questions in the History of Our Party (1981)

findings.claim: 'Deng was accused of treating the party like a card game: ‘black cat or white cat, so long as it catches mice’.'
findings.truth: The cat saying is Deng's own remark of 1962, quoted approvingly by him and only later used against him. It was not an accusation made about him, and it has nothing to do with his bridge playing.

findings.claim: Takeaway: 'Lin Biao’s ‘Bombard the Headquarters’ speech licensed attacks on the ‘four olds’ and on the CCP itself.'
findings.truth: 'Bombard the Headquarters' was Mao's own big-character poster of 5 August 1966 — as the same lesson's content and knowledge check both say. Lin Biao's contribution was the 18 August rally speech calling for the destruction of the four olds.
findings.evidence: internal contradiction with the lesson's content_html and knowledge check 3

findings.claim: 'the Cultural Revolution Group around Jiang Qing, Chen Boda and Kang Sheng issued the May 16 Notification'.
findings.truth: The Politburo issued the Notification, and the Notification created the Cultural Revolution Group — exactly as lesson 9 states. Cause and effect were inverted.

findings.claim: 'Liu Shaoqi was paraded in a dunce cap at a Tsinghua University rally' (1966), repeated as a flashcard question.
findings.truth: The Tsinghua mass rally was the humiliation of Liu's wife Wang Guangmei, on 10 April 1967, in a qipao and a necklace of ping-pong balls. Liu himself was denounced as a 'capitalist roader' and struggled against in 1967, but not at that rally.

findings.claim: Deaths 'with most occurring in 1966–68 and again in 1967–71 when the army imposed order'.
findings.truth: The two phases are given as overlapping ranges. The army-led purge phase (Cleansing the Class Ranks) runs 1968–71.

findings.claim: Hua Guofeng described as 'an industrial Hunanese cadre'.
findings.truth: Hua's provincial record was in agriculture and party administration in Hunan, not industry.

findings.claim: 'Jiang Qing ... the only woman in the senior leadership'; the exam tip's 'the male-only Politburo'; and a flashcard asking who was 'the only woman in the senior CCP leadership during the Cultural Revolution'.
findings.truth: Ye Qun sat on the Politburo alongside Jiang Qing from 1969 to 1971, and the lesson itself names Soong Ching-ling and Deng Yingchao as senior figures two sentences later. 'Male-only Politburo' also contradicts Jiang Qing's own membership.

findings.claim: 'The 1958 introduction of simplified characters reduced the strokes needed...'.
findings.truth: Pinyin was adopted in 1958; the first simplified-character scheme was published in 1956 and standardised in 1964 — as the lesson's own glossary entry says.
findings.evidence: internal contradiction with the lesson's glossary_terms

findings.claim: Key fact: 'schools and universities closed 1966–77 with gaokao abolished'.
findings.truth: The lesson body says universities reopened from 1970 (admission by class background, no entrance exam) and that village literacy classes mostly continued. Only the gaokao was gone for the whole 1966–77 span.
findings.evidence: internal contradiction with the lesson's content_html

findings.claim: Three Antis: 'Around 4,500,000 government employees were investigated ... an estimated 4,500 were executed.'
findings.truth: Neither figure could be confirmed, and the near-identical digits look like a corrupted pair. The Wikipedia article on the campaigns gives no investigation or execution total. Left unedited under the rule that a fact is only corrected when the true value is found; worth a second pass with a print source.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia 'Three-anti and Five-anti Campaigns' (no such figures)

findings.claim: 'The campaign against counter-revolutionaries opened in February 1951', while the key fact, the takeaway and a flashcard all frame it as 1950–52.
findings.truth: The campaign was launched by the October 1950 directive and hardened with the February 1951 Regulations. Both datings are defensible; the lesson uses them inconsistently.

findings.claim: Flashcard: 'Where did the slogan ‘Let a hundred flowers bloom’ come from?' — 'A classical Chinese poem'.
findings.truth: The second half of the slogan alludes to the Hundred Schools of Thought of the Warring States period rather than to a single poem. Sources differ on whether to call the source a poem, so left as written.

findings.claim: 'By the end of 1956, around 96% of peasant households had been pushed into higher-stage cooperatives' (repeated in a knowledge check and a flashcard).
findings.truth: By the end of 1956 about 96 per cent of households were in cooperatives of some kind; roughly 88 per cent were in higher-stage ones. GCSE textbooks routinely print the 96 per cent figure in this form, so it is left alone.

findings.claim: 'Around 60 million peasants were diverted from the harvest' to backyard furnaces (repeated four times in the lesson).
findings.truth: Estimates run from 60 million to 90 million depending on whether part-time labour is counted; 60 million is within the published range.
findings.evidence: Great Leap Forward steel campaign estimates

findings.claim: 'roughly 8,000 reached Yan’an in October 1935'.
findings.truth: The First Front Army reached northern Shaanxi in October 1935; the CCP only moved its headquarters to Yan'an in December 1936. The shorthand is standard in GCSE resources.

findings.claim: The First Five-Year Plan was 'run on the Chinese side by Premier Zhou Enlai, finance specialist Chen Yun and Liu Shaoqi'.
findings.truth: Zhou Enlai and Chen Yun are right; the third planner was Li Fuchun at the State Planning Commission rather than Liu Shaoqi. Not mark-affecting for this option's bullets.

findings.claim: 'Deng Xiaoping was sent to a Jiangxi tractor factory', placed inside the 1966–67 narrative.
findings.truth: Deng was sent to the Xinjian County tractor factory in Jiangxi in 1969. Lesson 11 dates it correctly.

summary: Fourteen lessons checked against Option 32 and the Paper 3 assessment section. The narrative history is strong: campaign dates, casualty ranges, the Lushan and Lin Biao sequences, the famine estimates and the 1976 endgame all hold up. The damage is concentrated in the exam furniture and in attribution. Every lesson taught the interpretation essay as a 20-mark question with a 16–20 top band, five exam tips repeated that error, and nineteen sentences invented claims about what examiners reward, twice citing examiner reports. Seven factual errors carry marks: the 1981 Resolution's 70/30 verdict applied to the Cultural Revolution, 'Bombard the Headquarters' credited to Lin Biao in a takeaway, the Cultural Revolution Group issuing the directive that created it, Wang Guangmei's Tsinghua humiliation given to Liu Shaoqi, the Huaihai start date, Deng's cat saying turned into an accusation, and simplified characters dated to 1958. 79 edits.
